A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VITAL research work and contain readable main text and complete appendices. Equations, tables, figures, and experiments can be matched reliably across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-visualization experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–5, ablations, and human studies with 58 and 42 participants.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds reference-selection, contamination, test-reference, and CIFAR-10 results in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: The distribution-matching objective, relevance weighting, regularization, transparency maps, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Cluster-based reference selection is examined as an additional sampling analysis; the stated default visualization procedure is retained.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds CIFAR-10 class visualization and a scenario involving reference images contaminated with out-of-class examples. The existing ImageNet class, intermediate-neuron, concept-visualization, and human-study coverage is retained. Using test-set references is a split change assessed under E3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged, including Fourier, MACO, DeepInversion, and PII where applicable. The new CIFAR-10 comparison reuses Fourier. Newly cited CRP and AttnLRP appear as future directions, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols use test-set references, cluster-conditioned references for three ImageNet classes, and contamination by adding 5, 10, or 20 out-of-class images. Figure 17 specifies 10 clusters and 50 nearest-neighbor references per cluster. Existing evaluation metrics, model configurations, and human-study designs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 substantially expands the analysis of reference dependence beyond v1's sample-size sweep and discussion of unstructured sampling. New experiments examine within-class mode coverage, training-versus-test references, cross-dataset generalization, and contamination robustness through Figures 13 and 17 and Table 6. These probe several previously untested dependencies of the reference-based approach.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose three random seeds for the existing visualization experiments and retain the same human-study distributions, medians, and quantiles. v2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the existing human-study results are unchanged. Table 6 adds results for new settings: CIFAR-10 CLIP top-1 accuracy is 78.30 for VITAL versus 11.40 for Fourier, while Corrupt-20 yields FID 113.30 and CLIP top-1 accuracy 47.30. Figures 13 and 17 add contamination examples and cluster-conditioned visualizations.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–4, sort-matching reasoning, and runtime complexity statement are unchanged. The new distribution-matching illustration adds explanation, not a formal result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: feature-distribution alignment and relevance weighting produce more interpretable visualizations across architectures and help interpret neural circuits. Rewording and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new clustering analysis as preserving within-class semantic diversity and the test-reference/CIFAR-10 results as supporting applicability beyond the original training data. It also discusses degradation under contaminated references while claiming useful residual stability. Existing limitations concerning spatial structure, realism, and human evaluation remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents reference construction for the added analyses, including 10 clusters, 50 nearest-neighbor images per cluster, and the numbers of out-of-class images added. Existing optimizer, regularization, runtime, and code-access disclosures remain unchanged; CIFAR-specific implementation details are sparse.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to concept relevance propagation and AttnLRP, connecting them to future neuron selection and transformer visualization. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against feature-visualization and model-inversion methods are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Several method, evaluation, discussion, and conclusion passages are shortened or rephrased, and Appendix C.4 gains explanatory paragraphs. The overall section order, terminology, and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a distribution-matching schematic (Figure 3), contamination examples (Figure 13), cluster-conditioned visualizations (Figure 17), and Table 6. Existing displays are retained with renumbering and local relocation, including Table 1 and the demographic plot; the overall visual design is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added reference-selection and contamination experiments address practical uncertainties left by v1, while the new schematic clarifies distribution matching. These provide useful additional validation without changing the principal comparative or human-study evidence. The gain is limited by the narrow CIFAR-10 comparison, which includes only Fourier, and sparse documentation of its specific setup.
